footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines ($532K in 2025). Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 40.0% to $152M in 2025. Net interest income rose 47.2% to $123M and noninterest income rose 15.7% to $28.6M; noninterest expense rose 42.2%, and the provision for credit losses was $5.3M, versus −$2.4M.
Net income rose 16.3% to $37.1M, or $3.60 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 66.3% versus 65.2%. ACNB returned $25.5M through dividends and buybacks.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: ACNB Corporation Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
